brief: UBS says politics has overtaken macro as the near-term equity driver after a Democratic sweep shifts debate toward AI/data-center regulation and permitting rather than purely Fed/inflation risk, even as UBS Economics still expects the Fed biased toward 25bp hikes in December and January unless labour deteriorates. 2027 AI demand visibility stays strong (cloud growth accelerating to 97% in 2027, DC vacancy below 2%), but top-13 hyperscaler capex of $1.77tn against $1.47tn operating cash flow implies a ~$300bn funding gap, making the opportunity more selective. Tighter DC regulation could raise electrical/cooling content per MW, favoring AI Industrials suppliers. Thursday's selloff (SPX -4.7%, NDX -6.4%, SOXX -12.2%, VIX +12pts) marked rotation becoming correlated index-level de-risking, but UBS says Q3 EPS growth of +31.6% and an 8,100 year-end SPX target argue this is a correction inside an uptrend, not a recession signal. UBS flags 2027 earnings inflections across Rivian, Amgen, Vertex, StandardAero, Packaging Corp and Kontoor as underpriced, while crowded positioning reversed sharply: hedge funds entered the midterms bearish USD only for a safe-haven rally to hit them, and China Tech short-covering turned it into a relative winner.
